test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: One pipe can fill the tank in 8 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 11 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill three-fourth of the tank?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net filling efficiency per minute = (1/8 − 1/11) = 3/88 of the tank.

Time to fill full tank = 88/3 minutes.

Time to fill 3/4th tank = (88/3) × (3/4) = 22 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling pipe time = 8 min, Emptying pipe time = 11 min.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = LCM of time taken; Efficiency = Work ÷ Time.

 
 **Pipe Type** **Time (min)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 Inlet Pipe (+) 8 88 units +11 
 Outlet Pipe (−) 11 −8 

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes = 11 − 8 = 3 units/min.

⇒ Required work = 3/4 of Total Capacity = 3/4 × 88 = 66 units.

⇒ Time required = Required work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time = 66 ÷ 3 = 22 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Convention

Inlet pipes that fill the tank are taken as positive efficiency, while outlet pipes that empty the tank are taken as negative efficiency.

Net Time Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours (y > x), net time to fill the tank = (xy) ÷ (y − x).

Work and Time Relationship

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. For a constant work, efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken.</p
